packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-07 -- unverified blind image reading (UTF-8 plain text)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this packet. I did not read packet.json. Only PROMPT.md, the brief, and the images in packet-07 were opened.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face 1; 1800x1201 reduced)
- Observation: not a page but a mounting of many narrow lozenge/spindle-shaped parchment strips (binding strips, cut with pointed ends), taped onto paper/plastic carriers, photographed on black with colour checker and cm scale (approx 38 cm visible).
- Group A (upper left): a large blank sheet of paper (no text) with a grey redaction/label bar; below it a row of 14 vertical strips (~9-10 cm long, ~1.5 cm wide) hanging from tape. Each strip carries short line-fragments of a cursive documentary-looking Gothic hand written ACROSS the strip, so each strip shows only 1-3 words per line, ~10-12 lines per strip. Visible words at this scale include "Symon", "apptatn(?)", "Stef", "nobis", "nomin(e)", "plena", "Comp(er)ente(?)", "appellant(?)".
- Group B (upper right): label "Stams, STA, Fr. 87-1" on a paper band; 8 strips (4 above, 4 below the band), same kind of cursive, again 1-2 words per line.
- Group C (lower right): label "Stams, STA, Frg. 87-2r(?)" ; ~15 strips taped in a row, mostly blank in this view; only top ends carry a few words ("Sabaudie"?, "Januar", "apud", "feendo"?), plus a pen flourish/signum-like mark near lower left of first strips, and "Ab Ju..."(?) near lower right strip. Blue modern pencil/ink writing on the tape ("apud Pont..." in blue) is modern annotation, not original.
- No columns, running titles, rubrics or enlarged initials discernible; script appears to be a single cursive hand with abbreviations. Tentative interpretation only: documentary or notarial prose cut into strips; lines on adjacent strips may or may not join (strip order on the mount need not be original).
- Limitations: because each strip shows only a few letters of each line, connected text across >2-3 words is not recoverable unless adjacent strips join; I transcribe per strip, top to bottom, strips counted left to right within each tile.
- Tile plan (inferred from dimensions): face 1 tiles image-002..006 (top row), 007..011 (middle row), 012..016 (bottom row); image-017 = overview of face 2 with tiles 018..029 (4x3); image-030 = overview of face 3 with tiles 031..042 (4x3).

=== image-007 (face 1, middle row, leftmost tile): first 4 strips of Group A (strip 4 cut at right edge) ===
Note: lines are counted per strip from the top of the strip. Hand: cursive Gothic (documentary cursive), long s, looped d, "z"-like 9/us sign (bz = b(us)), ꝑ/ꝓ-type p-abbreviations, frequent superscript strokes. Blue writing on the tape across the tops of strips 1-3 ("...quadri..." / "...ime...") is modern annotation, not transcribed as text.
Strips 2 and 3 appear to join: the word "huiusmodi" (line 3) runs across the gap between them, so they were probably adjacent in the original sheet.

image-007 strip 1:
 l1  [cut/illegible, under tape]
 l2  -ſimo qu-  (blue modern ink overlaps after "qu")
 l3  e?ciam n-   (etiam/eciam?)
 l4  causam
 l5  ꝑ(?) Stef-   (the first sign is a ß-like abbreviation; could be p(ro)/d(omi)n(u)s?)
 l6  mea a-
 l7  quibz (quib(us)) b-
 l8  dictum
 l9  Symon-
 l10 appllat- (appellat-, abbreviation stroke)
 l11 huius  (cut at bottom point)

image-007 strip 2:
 l1  [under tape] -ote(?)
 l2  ꝑ? eud-? (or "cud-")
 l3  appllon hu-  (appell(ati)on(em) hu-; continues on strip 3 "-iusmodi")
 l4  p?mrit(?)/puriti(?)  [uncertain]
 l5  -[..]tion(em) ꝯmiss(?) (commiss-?)
 l6  [..]n? fuit?/ut
 l7  Regerum(?) / -re geru-?
 l8  ſindicos (sindicos)
 l9  Ep(iscop)o p(ar)te i(n)?
 l10 que s(?) [illegible]
 l11 [flourish/descender only]

image-007 strip 3:
 l1  [under tape] -ime(?) (blue modern ink nearby)
 l2  ꝑ Stef-
 l3  -iusmodi (completes "hu-iusmodi" from strip 2)
 l4  -ncius non/nom-
 l5  -a? i(n) vos(?)
 l6  requisitus (r(e)quisitus?)
 l7  olim po-
 l8  gaudes?/gauder?  [uncertain]
 l9  ꝓhem- (p(ro)hem-?/ p(er)hem-?) [uncertain]
 l10 -ata s(?)
 l11 [illegible]

image-007 strip 4 (right edge cut by tile; continues on image-008):
 l1  -manu c-
 l2  Indictio-
 l3  -y? etia(m) c-
 l4  -m velin?/velut? 
 l5  -bz (-b(us)) appll- (appell-)
 l6  -m quelo-/querel-? 
 l7  -oce? ut al-
 l8  -m p(re)dict-
 l9  -ctos dict-
 l10 -ere cerre?/erce? [uncertain]
 l11 P[...]?  (stain)
 l12 -on ce-?

=== image-008 (face 1, middle row, tile 2) ===
Overlap: the leftmost strip here is image-007 strip 4 (repeated, not new text). New strips are numbered 5-9 (strip 9 cut at right edge).
Observation: strips 5-8 sit close together and several words visibly continue from one strip to the next across the same line (e.g. line 7 "p(re)fatum d(omi)n(u)m"), so these strips seem to preserve their original order and give short runs across a line. I give each line ACROSS strips 5-9, with " | " marking a strip boundary (a gap of a few letters may be lost at each cut).

 l2  s5 -sp(er)acta(?)/specta(?) | s6 -e dict(us)/dicti(?) | s7 Joha(nnes?) | s8 ꝑ ygez(?)/ꝑ yg- [uncertain] | s9 -i(n)tere(?)-

 l5  s5 -ns iusta-/iusti- | s6 D(?)sprectum(?) vre (v(est)re?) [uncertain] | s7 -vre?/ | s8 -uns(?) -bz (-ib(us)) | s9 -um om-

 l10 s5 -vect(?) & | s6 C?oz/Cos zre(?) | s7 -m tenor- | s8 -ey/-en | s9 -rumq(ue)(?)
 l11 s5 -et ... | s6 Die n-/dic(t)e n- | s7 -cerat-/-teram(?) | s8 -rant/-vant | s9 -...
 l12 s9 Ito(?)/bo- [illegible]
Running text recoverable from line 7: "... p(re)fatum d(omi)n(u)m Ber[...]um Iud[...]" ; line 9: "...noibus a[...]et vniu(er)sitate(m) et h[...]is dict(us)..." ; line 3: "nobis d[...]tis nominib(us) consti[...]tum".
